===== WORLD 23 · LESSON position_and_chart · Position and chart =====

TASK w23_1_teach [theory] What must be true before you apply an unopened chart row?
CAPTION: Range construction begins with seat, the verified action prefix, depth and size. Use the published Sharky chart only for the covered configurations.
TEACH: What must be true before you apply an unopened chart row? Range construction begins with seat, the verified action prefix, depth and size. Use the published Sharky chart only for the covered configurations.
Q: What must be true before you apply an unopened chart row?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] Everybody before your seat has folded, and that seat is covered — Correct. A limp or raise creates a different prefix. Verify the position and stack scope first.
  - [wrong] At least one player has already raised — Look again. This is a response-to-open situation.
    BETTER ANSWER: Everybody before your seat has folded, and that seat is covered
  - [wrong] Any player has matched the big blind voluntarily — Look again. A limp enters the pot and removes the unopened condition.
    BETTER ANSWER: Everybody before your seat has folded, and that seat is covered

===== WORLD 23 · LESSON notations_and_hand_families · Notations and hand families =====

TASK w23_2_teach [theory] What distinguishes a wheel ace from another suited ace?
CAPTION: Read suited, offsuit and pair notation separately. Compare high-card value, straight connectivity and which complete hands can be strongest.
TEACH: What distinguishes a wheel ace from another suited ace? Read suited, offsuit and pair notation separately. Compare high-card value, straight connectivity and which complete hands can be strongest.
Q: What distinguishes a wheel ace from another suited ace?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] The lower card is 2 through 5, supporting A-2-3-4-5 — Correct. The ace can act low for that straight and retains the suited-ace flush feature.
  - [wrong] The cards must be offsuit — Look again. Wheel potential depends on the ranks. Suit changes other properties.
    BETTER ANSWER: The lower card is 2 through 5, supporting A-2-3-4-5
  - [wrong] It is already a made straight preflop — Look again. A two-card hand still needs three community ranks to complete one.
    BETTER ANSWER: The lower card is 2 through 5, supporting A-2-3-4-5

TASK w23_2_read_notation_after_blocker [drill] How many combos of each remain?
CAPTION: Compare AQs and AQo with Q♦ in your hand. No ace is known, and no board has been dealt.
Q: How many combos of each remain?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You Qd Jd | Pot 1.5 BB | To call 1 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO folded stack 100 BB | BTN dealer Qd Jd stack 100 BB | SB stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 99 BB
TRAIL: preflop: SB posts 0.5 BB · preflop: BB posts 1 BB · preflop: UTG folds · preflop: HJ folds · preflop: CO folds
  + [correct] 3 suited and 9 offsuit — Correct. Three queens survive. Each matches one ace in suit and three in different suits.
  - [wrong] 4 suited and 12 offsuit — Look again. Those are unblocked counts. One queen is known.
    BETTER ANSWER: 3 suited and 9 offsuit
  - [wrong] 3 suited and 12 offsuit — Look again. The known queen removes one suited pairing and three offsuit pairings.
    BETTER ANSWER: 3 suited and 9 offsuit

===== WORLD 23 · LESSON opener_size_and_defense · Opener size and defense =====

TASK w23_3_teach [theory] What changes when BTN makes it 2 BB instead of 2.5 BB and SB folds?
CAPTION: Open size means the total of the first voluntary raise. A smaller open needs less extra from the big blind. Immediate price is one input. Realization, the opening range and players remaining can change what actually defends profitably.
TEACH: What changes when BTN makes it 2 BB instead of 2.5 BB and SB folds? Open size means the total of the first voluntary raise. A smaller open needs less extra from the big blind. Immediate price is one input. Realization, the opening range and players remaining can change what actually defends profitably.
Q: What changes when BTN makes it 2 BB instead of 2.5 BB and SB folds?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] The big blind owes less and needs a smaller showdown share in a terminal model — Correct. Compute the extra payment after the posted blind and divide by the final pot.
  - [wrong] The big blind pays the full open size in either branch — Look again. The posted big blind already counts toward the target.
    BETTER ANSWER: The big blind owes less and needs a smaller showdown share in a terminal model
  - [wrong] The smaller open creates a higher call-equity threshold — Look again. The target and pot both change. The smaller call costs a smaller fraction here.
    BETTER ANSWER: The big blind owes less and needs a smaller showdown share in a terminal model

TASK w23_3_read_bb_minraise [drill] What is the immediate price?
CAPTION: BTN opens to 2 BB and SB folds. BB decides with the posted 1 BB already in the pot.

  + [correct] 22.2% — Correct. The extra 1 BB adds to a final pot of 4.5 BB.
  - [wrong] 25% — Look again. That leaves out the folded small blind.
    BETTER ANSWER: 22.2%
  - [wrong] 44.4% — Look again. That counts the entire raise target as a new payment, ignoring the 1 BB already posted.
    BETTER ANSWER: 22.2%

TASK w23_3_guided_bb_two_sizes_compare [drill] Which threshold goes with the 2.5 BB open?

TEACH: Which threshold goes with the 2.5 BB open? Subtract the blind already paid, then include the caller’s new chips in the denominator.

  + [correct] 27.3% — Correct. BB adds 1.5 BB to a final pot of 5.5 BB. The 2 BB opening branch needs only 22.2%.
  - [wrong] 22.2% — Look again. That price applies to a match to 2 BB.
    BETTER ANSWER: 27.3%
  - [wrong] 33.3% — Look again. Using 1.5 divided by a truncated pot omits chips from the terminal comparison.

TASK w23_3_transfer_open_size_buys_folds [drill] Which open has the better zero-recovery comparison?
CAPTION: BTN is first in. A proposed 2 BB open and a proposed 3 BB open make both blinds fold in the same 6 of 10 equally weighted branches. In the four called branches assign zero recovery solely for this risk comparison.
Q: Which open has the better zero-recovery comparison?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You Ad Qd | Pot 1.5 BB | To call 1 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO folded stack 100 BB | BTN dealer Ad Qd stack 100 BB | SB stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 99 BB
TRAIL: preflop: SB posts 0.5 BB · preflop: BB posts 1 BB · preflop: UTG folds · preflop: HJ folds · preflop: CO folds
  + [correct] 2 BB — Correct. Both sizes win the same 1.5 BB in the same six branches. The 2 BB size loses less in all four remaining branches.
  - [wrong] 3 BB — Look again. A larger risk can be justified by more folds or better called payoff. Neither is supplied.
    BETTER ANSWER: 2 BB
  - [wrong] Both sizes earn the same because the fold rate ties — Look again. The failed branches cost one BB more at the larger size.
    BETTER ANSWER: 2 BB

TASK w23_3_day7_different_prices_different_calls [review] What is best at the current size?
ENTRY: drill
CAPTION: BTN opens to 3 BB and SB folds. In 100 equally weighted terminal outcomes, you win 27 and lose 73. Holding that share fixed, also consider a 2 BB opening size.
Q: What is best at the current size?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You 7s 6s | Pot 4.5 BB | To call 2 BB | Seat BB | Active bb | Decision bb | Facts no applicable hand facts
EFFECTIVE: BTN 100
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO folded stack 100 BB | BTN dealer stack 97 BB raise 3 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB 7s 6s stack 99 BB
TRAIL: preflop: SB posts 0.5 BB · preflop: BB posts 1 BB · preflop: UTG folds · preflop: HJ folds · preflop: CO folds · preflop: BTN raises to 3 BB · preflop: SB folds
  + [correct] Fold now. Call would work against the 2 BB counterfactual. — Correct. Fold because your 27% misses the price of calling the current 3 BB BTN open. Against the 2 BB open, the same share clears the cheaper price.
  - [wrong] Call at both sizes — Look again. At 3 BB, 27% of the 6.5 BB final pot falls short of the 2 BB cost.
    BETTER ANSWER: Fold now. Call would work against the 2 BB counterfactual.
  - [wrong] Fold at both sizes — Look again. At the lower price 27% of 4.5 BB exceeds the 1 BB cost.
    BETTER ANSWER: Fold now. Call would work against the 2 BB counterfactual.

===== WORLD 23 · LESSON three_four_five_bet · Three four five bet =====

TASK w23_4_teach [theory] When is a 5-bet shove a value action?
CAPTION: Choose re-raises around weaker paying hands, better folds and stack commitments. A 5-bet is the raise after a 4-bet. When it is all-in, a call ends preflop betting heads-up.
TEACH: When is a 5-bet shove a value action? Choose re-raises around weaker paying hands, better folds and stack commitments. A 5-bet is the raise after a 4-bet. When it is all-in, a call ends preflop betting heads-up.
Q: When is a 5-bet shove a value action?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] When the stated weaker continuations make paying the remaining stack worthwhile — Correct. The re-raise number names the action. The opponent response supplies the value.
  - [wrong] Every time the shove is larger than an opening raise — Look again. The name and size do not guarantee a profitable caller range.
    BETTER ANSWER: When the stated weaker continuations make paying the remaining stack worthwhile
  - [wrong] Only when no hand could fold — Look again. A value shove can still induce folds from some hands.
    BETTER ANSWER: When the stated weaker continuations make paying the remaining stack worthwhile

TASK w23_4_read_raise_number [drill] What is the name of BTN’s proposed final raise?
CAPTION: CO opens to 2.5 BB, BTN makes it 8 BB, and CO makes it 22 BB after the blinds fold. BTN may now raise all-in.
Q: What is the name of BTN’s proposed final raise?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Preflop | You As Ks | Pot 31.5 BB | To call 14 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Facts no applicable hand facts
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO stack 78 BB raise 22 BB | BTN dealer As Ks stack 92 BB raise 8 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB folded stack 99 BB
TRAIL: preflop: SB posts 0.5 BB · preflop: BB posts 1 BB · preflop: UTG folds · preflop: HJ folds · preflop: CO raises to 2.5 BB · preflop: BTN raises to 8 BB · preflop: SB folds · preflop: BB folds · preflop: CO raises to 22 BB
  + [correct] A 5-bet shove — Correct. The big blind counts as the initial bet. The raise after the 4-bet is a 5-bet.
  - [wrong] A 4-bet shove — Look again. CO’s raise to 22 BB was already the 4-bet.
    BETTER ANSWER: A 5-bet shove
  - [wrong] A call of 22 BB — Look again. Calling pays the difference to 22 BB. Raising all-in above that total increases the wager.
    BETTER ANSWER: A 5-bet shove

TASK w23_4_transfer_five_bet_price_flips [drill] Which response earns most at the current stack depth?
CAPTION: You 4-bet to 22 BB and BTN raises all-in to the effective 35 BB. BTN’s all-in range is equally weighted legal AA KK AKo. Both players started with 35 BB. At 100 BB compare a full 100 BB all-in with the same range and unchanged earlier action.

  + [correct] Call 13 BB — Correct. Call because your jacks have 37.8% equity against BTN’s stated range, above the shorter all-in’s 18.2% price. Folding gives up positive expected value.
  - [wrong] Fold because 22 BB was already invested — Look again. Past chips help form the pot. Calling earns positive expected value at the current price; folding gives up that gain.

  - [wrong] Call at both stack depths — Look again. The same equity is below the deeper threshold. Matching the full 100 BB stack costs more.

===== WORLD 24 · LESSON polar_and_condensed · Polar and condensed =====

TASK w24_1_teach [theory] What distinguishes the two shapes?
CAPTION: Strong value means hands likely to beat the calling range. A polar betting range combines strong value with bluffs. A condensed range consists mostly of middle-strength hands. A bluff catcher is a hand that loses to value bets but beats bluffs. Middle hands may catch bluffs profitably if the price and bluff share allow.
TEACH: What distinguishes the two shapes? Strong value means hands likely to beat the calling range. A polar betting range combines strong value with bluffs. A condensed range consists mostly of middle-strength hands. A bluff catcher is a hand that loses to value bets but beats bluffs. Middle hands may catch bluffs profitably if the price and bluff share allow.

  - [wrong] Whether the pot was opened preflop — Look again. Either range shape can arise after different earlier actions.
    BETTER ANSWER: Where strong hands, middle hands and misses are concentrated

TEACH: What fold rate breaks even when bluffing B into pot P with no recovery? For a zero-equity bluff, alpha means the break-even fold rate. MDF is its complement. A call has a different threshold since the final pot includes the matched bet and call.

  - [wrong] P/(P+B) — Look again. That is the continuation frequency that makes the bluff break even.

===== WORLD 24 · LESSON value_bluff_balance · Value bluff balance =====

TASK w24_3_teach [theory] For a pot-sized bet, what value-to-bluff ratio makes such a caller indifferent?
CAPTION: A bluff catcher is indifferent when the betting range’s bluff share equals the call price, assuming it loses to every value bet and beats every bluff. A balanced range is a mix of value bets and bluffs chosen so the opponent’s bluff catcher breaks even at the offered price. Translate that share into a ratio or a weighted combo count.
TEACH: For a pot-sized bet, what value-to-bluff ratio makes such a caller indifferent? A bluff catcher is indifferent when the betting range’s bluff share equals the call price, assuming it loses to every value bet and beats every bluff. A balanced range is a mix of value bets and bluffs chosen so the opponent’s bluff catcher breaks even at the offered price. Translate that share into a ratio or a weighted combo count.
Q: For a pot-sized bet, what value-to-bluff ratio makes such a caller indifferent?

===== WORLD 24 · LESSON thin_value_and_check · Thin value and check =====

TASK w24_5_teach [theory] What is the first question when considering a thin value raise?
CAPTION: A thin bet or raise earns a modest edge from worse calls. A backdoor draw is a draw that needs two future board cards to complete. At the river, payoffs can be compared by counting extra chips from weaker hands, extra losses to better calls and bluffs that stop paying.
TEACH: What is the first question when considering a thin value raise? A thin bet or raise earns a modest edge from worse calls. A backdoor draw is a draw that needs two future board cards to complete. At the river, payoffs can be compared by counting extra chips from weaker hands, extra losses to better calls and bluffs that stop paying.
Q: What is the first question when considering a thin value raise?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] Which worse hands call the raise? — Correct. Sometimes the existing small bet already captures value from weaker hands that would fold to a raise.
  - [wrong] Does the hand have a backdoor draw? — Look again. The river leaves no future cards.
    BETTER ANSWER: Which worse hands call the raise?
  - [wrong] Can the opponent call regardless of what they hold? — Look again. Possible callers are a subset of the legal two-card combinations. Use the supplied response.
    BETTER ANSWER: Which worse hands call the raise?

TASK w24_5_read_what_thin_raise_costs [drill] What must justify the extra raised chips?

TASK w24_6_teach [theory] What makes a river check-raise bluff feasible?
CAPTION: A river check-raise needs a terminal value or bluff payoff. Compare the bet range, the continuing subset and how much a failed raise costs.
TEACH: What makes a river check-raise bluff feasible? A river check-raise needs a terminal value or bluff payoff. Compare the bet range, the continuing subset and how much a failed raise costs.
Q: What makes a river check-raise bluff feasible?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] The bettor has enough hands that can fold to the raise — Correct. The raise needs more than a blocker. If the bet range is already too strong and never folds, a pure bluff fails.
  - [wrong] A chance to improve on the next card — Look again. There are no remaining cards after this street.
    BETTER ANSWER: The bettor has enough hands that can fold to the raise
  - [wrong] An earlier check that proves weakness — Look again. A check can retain strong hands. The opponent’s response still decides the raise’s value.
    BETTER ANSWER: The bettor has enough hands that can fold to the raise
